workflows.name: Corporate Investigations: Fraud, Theft, Embezzlement & IP Misappropriation

Automation Opportunity: - Case-management workflow; digital-evidence preservation tools; cross-function allegation intake
Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: evidence preserved with chain-of-custody; Legal-privileged and rights-compliant (VS-91/VS-84); recovery/insurance pursued
Cross-references: - distinct from VS-23 (retail shrink); links to VS-21/VS-119/VS-125 (audit/ethics/fraud), VS-100.3/VS-100 (legal/prosecution), VS-26 (crime insurance), W4693 (evidence)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Evidence-spoliation risk**: Evidence not preserved → inadmissible / failed recovery; mitigated by immediate preservation and chain-of-custody (W4693)
- **Privilege/legal-misstep risk**: Investigation conducted outside Legal privilege or violating labor/privacy rights (VS-91/VS-84) → exposure; mitigated by Legal coordination
System Touchpoints: - Case management (security ops); whistleblower (VS-119); audit (VS-21); LP/fraud (VS-23/VS-125); digital forensics (VS-27.3); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Intake and triage allegations of corporate crime (executive/employee fraud, embezzlement, IP theft/trade-secret misappropriation, vendor collusion, bribery VS-86); assess credibility and scope; preserve evidence immediately

Conduct the investigation: interviews, digital forensics (with cyber VS-27.3), document review, surveillance (W4693) within legal limits; coordinate with Legal (privilege VS-100.3) and HR (discipline/termination VS-19)

Conclude with findings, recovery/restitution, discipline/termination (VS-19), insurance claim (VS-26 crime policy), and law-enforcement referral/prosecution (VS-100) where warranted; capture lessons (W4696)

fields.Participants: HR (VS-19/VS-103), IT/cyber (VS-27.3 — user-behavior analytics), Ethics (VS-119), Legal (VS-100.3)

fields.Volume: ~ indicators across ~6,762 employees + contingent (VS-98) + sensitive-role population

workflows.name: Insider-Threat Detection, Background Re-Check & Offboarding Risk

Automation Opportunity: - UBA + cross-function indicator correlation; background-re-check workflow; offboarding-access-revocation automation (VS-27)
Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: monitoring lawful and proportionate (VS-91/VS-84); sensitive-role re-checks; offboarding access revoked
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (people analytics), VS-27.3 (cyber/UBA/access), VS-119 (ethics), VS-19 W43 (offboarding), VS-91/VS-84 (privacy/labor)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Missed-indicator risk**: Insider-threat indicators in disparate systems not correlated → undetected risk; mitigated by cross-function intake and UBA
- **Privacy/labor-rights risk**: Insider-threat monitoring exceeding lawful bounds → VS-91/VS-84 exposure; mitigated by Legal/HR governance and proportionality
System Touchpoints: - HR/people analytics (VS-103); cyber UBA (VS-27.3); ethics (VS-119); access management (VS-27.3); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Operate insider-threat detection: indicators from HR (performance/behavior/financial-stress VS-103), cyber (data-exfiltration/user-behavior analytics VS-27.3), ethics (VS-119), and access patterns; assess for espionage, sabotage, fraud, or workplace-violence potential

Conduct background re-checks for sensitive roles (finance, treasury VS-18, data/privacy, security, executive support) and on indicators; manage offboarding-risk (W43 separation) — access revocation, exit interviews, data-handling review
Intervene proportionately (support, monitoring, role change, discipline, law-enforcement referral) with Legal/HR/privacy safeguards (VS-91/VS-84); document and review

fields.Participants: HR (VS-19/VS-84), OH/EAP (VS-83), Legal (VS-100.3), management, law enforcement
fields.Trigger: Threat indicator (disgruntled employee, domestic-violence spillover, harassment VS-84, terminations)

Automation Opportunity: - Threat-assessment methodology workflow; cross-function indicator intake; discreet-manager-briefing tool
Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: structured threat assessment by multi-disciplinary team; proportionate intervention; discreet/privacy-compliant handling (VS-91)
Cross-references: - links to VS-19/VS-84 (HR/labor), VS-83 (OH/EAP), VS-19 W43 (termination), VS-91 (privacy), VS-150 (drug-free intersect)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-responded-threat risk**: A credible violence indicator not intervened → harm; mitigated by the structured methodology and multi-disciplinary team
- **Privacy/stigma risk**: Disclosure of an individual's mental-health/domestic situation breaching privacy (VS-91); mitigated by discreet, need-to-know handling
System Touchpoints: - Case management (security ops); HR/Labor (VS-19/VS-84); EAP/OH (VS-83); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Operate a multi-disciplinary Threat Assessment Team (security + HR + OH/EAP + Legal) for workplace-violence indicators; assess threat level using a structured methodology (proximity, intent, capability, stressors)

Intervene proportionately: EAP/counseling (VS-83), mediation, administrative leave, restraining order, enhanced security, law-enforcement referral; manage high-risk terminations (VS-19 W43) with security presence
De-escalate and monitor post-intervention; brief affected managers/workplaces discreetly; review and adjust on new information

workflows.name: Active-Assailant, Civil-Unrest & Protest / Crowd Response Protocol

Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: rehearsed protocols per site type; mass-notification tested; law-enforcement coordination
Cross-references: - links to VS-26 (BCP), VS-14.3 (crisis comms), VS-07/VS-04 (site ops), VS-83 (trauma/EAP), W4694 (incident response)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unprepared-site risk**: A site with unrehearsed protocols → chaotic, harmful response; mitigated by rehearsed protocols and drills
- **Mass-notification-failure risk**: Staff not alerted in time; mitigated by multi-channel mass notification and testing
System Touchpoints: - Emergency/mass-notification system; BCP (VS-26); comms (VS-14.3); site access control (W4677); records (VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~continuous preparedness (drills ~2–4×/yr per site type); per-incident all-consuming

steps.activity: Maintain and rehearse active-assailant/civil-unrest response protocols (run-hide-fight, lockdown, evacuation, shelter-in-place) for HQ, stores, DCs, and events; train staff and integrate with BCP (VS-26) and fire-drill programs
On incident: activate the protocol, alert law enforcement (W4693), execute lockdown/evacuation per the situation, account for people, and coordinate medical (VS-83) and crisis comms (VS-14.3)
Conduct post-incident review and trauma support (VS-83 EAP); coordinate with BCP (VS-26) for business resumption and with Legal/insurance (VS-100/VS-26) for liability

fields.Participants: Legal (VS-100.3), Privacy (VS-91), law enforcement (PNP/NBI/PNP-ACG), prosecutors, digital forensics (VS-27.3)

workflows.name: Surveillance, Evidence Collection & Coordination with Law Enforcement (PNP/NBI)

Automation Opportunity: - Evidence/chain-of-custody management system; lawful-surveillance-scoping rules; law-enforcement-liaison workflow
Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: surveillance/evidence lawful (VS-91/VS-100.3); chain-of-custody maintained; shared with law enforcement within legal limits
Cross-references: - links to W4677 (CCTV), VS-27.3 (forensics), VS-100/VS-100.3 (legal/prosecution), VS-91 (privacy), VS-88 (records)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unlawful-surveillance risk**: Surveillance/evidence collected unlawfully → inadmissible + liability (VS-91); mitigated by Legal governance and lawful scoping
- **Chain-of-custody-break risk**: Broken custody → inadmissible evidence; mitigated by documented chain-of-custody
System Touchpoints: - CCTV/evidence systems (W4677); digital forensics (VS-27.3); legal/matter management (VS-100); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Conduct lawful surveillance/evidence collection (CCTV W4677, digital forensics VS-27.3, document, witness) within legal/privacy limits (VS-91/VS-100.3); maintain chain-of-custody and evidence integrity
Coordinate with law enforcement (PNP/NBI) for criminal matters: report, share evidence, support investigation/prosecution (VS-100 legal ops); manage information-sharing within legal limits
Preserve evidence and the investigation record for litigation/prosecution (VS-100) and insurance (VS-26); manage privacy of subject/non-subject data (VS-91)

workflows.name: Security Incident Response, Crisis Management & Executive Notification

Automation Opportunity: - Incident-response activation workflow; executive-notification cascade; crisis-team coordination tools
Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: severity tiers + notification cascade; joint incident command; board notified per threshold (VS-36)
Cross-references: - links to VS-26 (BCP/insurance), VS-27.3 (cyber IR), VS-14.3 (comms), VS-36 (board), W4686 (K&R), W4696 (review)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-notification risk**: Executives/board informed late → poor decisions and governance failure (VS-36); mitigated by the notification cascade and thresholds
- **Fragmented-response risk**: Incident command fragmented across security/BCP/cyber/comms; mitigated by the framework and joint command
System Touchpoints: - Incident/crisis-response system; BCP (VS-26); comms (VS-14.3); board reporting (VS-36); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Maintain the security incident-response & crisis-management framework: severity tiers, crisis-response team, activation thresholds, executive-notification cascade, and board-notification protocol (VS-36)
steps.r: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

steps.activity: On a significant incident: activate the response, establish incident command (joint with BCP VS-26, cyber VS-27.3, comms VS-14.3), notify executives/board per threshold, and coordinate resources (law enforcement, insurance VS-26, medevac)
steps.r: CSO / Crisis Response Lead / Exec Team

steps.activity: Manage the crisis to resolution; coordinate post-incident review (W4696), insurance/recovery (VS-26), legal (VS-100), and stakeholder/board reporting (VS-36)
steps.r: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Legal / Insurance

fields.Trigger: Extortion attempt; smear/defamation campaign; coordinated attack (physical + reputational + cyber) on BuildRight or a principal

workflows.name: Executive & Corporate Extortion, Defamation & Coordinated-Attack Response

Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: converged response protocol; Legal-guided; law-enforcement engagement; no-concession posture per policy
Cross-references: - links to W4674 (protective intel), W4694 (incident response), VS-14.3 (crisis comms), VS-27.3 (cyber), VS-100.3/VS-86 (legal/ABC)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Converged-attack-blindness risk**: A coordinated physical+cyber+reputational attack handled in silos → ineffective response; mitigated by the converged protocol
- **Concession/legal risk**: Improper payment/response creating ABC or legal exposure (VS-86/VS-100.3); mitigated by Legal guidance and no-concession posture
System Touchpoints: - Crisis-response (W4694); protective intel (W4674); legal/matter (VS-100); comms (VS-14.3); cyber (VS-27.3)

steps.activity: Maintain the coordinated-attack/extortion/defamation response protocol: convergence of physical security, cyber, legal, and comms; law-enforcement engagement; and the no-concession posture where mandated by policy/law

On an extortion/defamation/coordinated-attack event: activate the response, assess credibility and intent (W4674), engage legal (cease-and-desist, prosecution VS-100) and crisis comms (VS-14.3), and coordinate with cyber (VS-27.3) for converged attacks
Manage to resolution; protect the principal/brand; conduct post-event review (W4696) and adjust intelligence, posture, and protocols

fields.Participants: Internal Audit (VS-21), Head of Internal Audit & Risk (VS-21.2), Board Risk Committee (VS-36), Op Excellence (VS-133)

workflows.name: Corporate Security Metrics, Assurance & Post-Incident Review

Automation Opportunity: - Security-metrics dashboards; post-incident-review workflow with corrective-action tracking
Controls: - CTL-709 (ensure controlled execution — Investigations, Insider Threat, Workplace Violence & Crisis Response (PA-159.3).)
- CTL-709: outcome-oriented KRIs reported to board; post-incident corrective actions tracked; program assured via VS-21
Cross-references: - links to VS-21/VS-21.2/VS-21.3 W358 (audit/ERM), VS-36 (board), VS-133 (op excellence), W4673 (strategy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-vanity risk**: Metrics that don't predict/effect outcomes → false assurance; mitigated by outcome-oriented KRIs tied to risk appetite (W4673)
- **Lessons-not-learned risk**: Post-incident reviews without corrective-action closure → recurrence; mitigated by tracked corrective actions (VS-133)
System Touchpoints: - Security metrics/analytics; ERM/KRIs (VS-21.2); audit (VS-21); board reporting (VS-36); op excellence (VS-133)
Time Estimate: - ~3–5 days/quarter metrics + reporting; per-incident review absorbed

steps.a: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Maintain corporate-security metrics & KRIs (threat-profile trends, incident frequency/severity, travel-risk exposure, investigation outcomes, EP/GSOC readiness, vendor performance); report to the Head of Internal Audit & Risk and board risk committee (VS-36)
Conduct post-incident reviews (after every significant incident) capturing root cause, response effectiveness, and corrective actions; feed corrective actions into the program and into VS-21/VS-133
steps.r: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Op Excellence

steps.a: CSO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Assure the program via Internal Audit (VS-21) and the physical-security audit (VS-21.3 W358); continuously improve (VS-133) and refresh the strategy (W4673)
